subject: Banking
title: Market Making Explained
description: A quick win: understand Market Making Explained.

hook.text: When you buy a stock, a market maker often sells it to you from its own inventory.

buildup.text: Market makers post bid and ask prices. The spread between them, often pennies per share, is their profit.

discovery.text: Without market makers, finding a buyer or seller would take time.

twist.text: Market makers can lose money in volatile markets when prices move against their inventory before they can adjust.

climax.text: Market making is the utility function of finance. It keeps markets liquid so everyone can trade when they want.

punchline.text: Pennies per share, millions of shares. Market makers enable instant trades.

quiz.question: How do market makers earn money?
options: The bid-ask spread on each share they buy and sell

details.summary: Market makers are firms that continuously quote buy and sell prices for securities, providing liquidity by always being willing to trade. They profit from the bid-ask spread, the small difference between buying and selling prices.
details.whyItMatters: Without market makers, you could not instantly buy or sell stocks. They ensure that markets function smoothly by absorbing temporary imbalances between buyers and sellers, though they take risk in the process.
takeaways: Market makers quote continuous buy and sell prices for securities
They profit from the bid-ask spread on each transaction
Major market makers handle trillions in daily trading volume

faq.question: How do market makers manage their risk?
faq.answer: They hedge positions continuously, maintain inventory limits, and use algorithms to adjust prices based on market conditions. In volatile markets, they widen spreads to compensate for increased risk of holding positions.

faq.question: Do market makers ever lose money?
faq.answer: Yes, during extreme market events. When markets crash, market makers can be stuck holding inventory that is rapidly losing value. The 2020 COVID crash and 2010 Flash Crash both caused significant market maker losses.
